_readme: FIAT GEAR - bags. 11 bases, one job each, written straight to the LIVE name art/items/<slug>.png ('single': one file, no _NN, no sheet, no _response.json). Each job's size is the base's footprint x 64 px (data.gd SIZE / FOOTPRINTS): the game draws the picture at its own pixels, centred, when it fits the cell.

Run: godot --headless --script res://tools/pixellab_batch_v2.gd ++ --manifest res://tools/pixellab_items_bags_manifest.json   (++ --dry-run to list). A job whose file exists is skipped, so a rerun only does what's missing; one that came out wrong: ++ --only <slug> ++ --force, or delete the file and rerun.
Items.slug(base) is the name: lowercase, runs of anything but a letter or digit become one underscore. The cells load the file if it exists and show text if not, so the pool fills in any order.

ORDER: run long_guns first - it has no style image. Promote three or four of the best and copy them to art/reference/items/ref_01.png .. ref_04.png; every other manifest rides those as style_image with every style option on, rotated, so the whole pool shares the guns' palette and rendering.
If the API refuses a wide aspect (a 5x1 gun is 320x64), regenerate at the same width and twice the height; the loader fits and centres it.
Regenerate these manifests with python3 tools/make_item_manifests.py after any footprint change.

jobs.description: A realistic painted pixel-art still-life of a single thin white supermarket carrier bag, the cheap crinkled plastic kind with two loop handles, standing upright as if set down on the floor, seen from the front, filling the frame, half full and sagging, the plastic stretched thin and translucent, a split patched with a strip of brown parcel tape. One object centred and filling the frame, soft directional overcast daylight, natural material rendering with fine detail and painterly shading; no black outlines, no flat cel shading, not anime, not a cartoon, not a glossy video-game item; the look of a real object photographed on a grey day in a country that has run out of money. Muted cool northern palette, worn and repaired, nothing new. Nothing else in the frame, no hands, no person, no text, no logos, a plain dark neutral background.
